Your black metal mix sounds this thin. I flipped it against the release master so you can hear exactly where.

▸ Width. I put 2.7 dB more into the sides, so the tremolo wall wraps around the vocals instead of sitting on them.
▸ Body. 160 to 630 Hz comes up 3 to 4 dB. That's where your riffs went missing.
▸ Level. -14 LUFS, true peak -1 dBTP. Streaming turns you down to about there anyway, so I don't push past it.

It's Frostbound Sepulchre by Vesper Mortis. Out in January.

What did you hear first, the width or the low mids?

polished.media

#blackmetal #mastering #metalmastering #mixingmastering #audioengineering

Your gothic metal mix: -18 LUFS.

That's where it starts. Quiet, and a bit hollow. You'll notice it when it flips: I brought 160 to 315 Hz up by 2.3 dB, and the whole song lands at -10.4 LUFS. I didn't widen it. Didn't need to, because the room was already there in your mix and I'd only have smeared it.

It's Velvet Requiem by Vesper Mortis.

Which did you hear first, the low mids or the level?

polished.media

#gothicmetal #mastering #metalmastering #mixingmastering #audioengineering

Your death metal mix sounds this thin. You'll hear it the second it flips.

I didn't touch the arrangement. I lifted 160 to 315 Hz by 2.5 dB, because that's where a death metal riff gets its weight, and I gave the sides 2.5 dB more room. Then it went from -17.4 to -8.8 LUFS. That's all.

It's Carrion Liturgy by Vesper Mortis.

What did you hear first, the width or the low mids?

polished.media

#deathmetal #mastering #metalmastering #mixingmastering #audioengineering

Your black metal mix: -19 LUFS.

I pulled 160 to 315 Hz up 4.4 dB, because that's where a black metal riff keeps its weight, and I gave the sides 2.6 dB more room so the wall opens up around the vocals.

Level goes from -18.7 LUFS on the mix to -12.7 on the master. Hear it again on the loop.

It's Hoarfrost Vigil by Vesper Mortis.

What did you hear first, the width or the low mids?

Same level. One is mastered.

No loudness trick here. I matched both clips to -13.6 LUFS before cutting this, so the only thing left to hear is what the master changed: 10000 to 16000 Hz comes down 3.6 dB and 160 to 315 Hz comes up 2.7 dB.

The answer shows up at 23 seconds.

It's Velvet Requiem by Vesper Mortis.

Did you pick A or B before the reveal?

#gothicmetal #mastering #metalmastering #mixingmastering #audioengineering

160 to 630 Hz, mix vs master.

Low mids only, first. For the first 14 seconds I only let 160 to 630 Hz through, both clips at the same overall level, and the master's got 3.9 dB more down there. That's the weight a thin death metal mix is missing.

Then I bring in the full song: your mix as delivered at -19.6 LUFS, my master at -10.4.

It's Carrion Liturgy by Vesper Mortis.

Was it easier to hear in the low mids alone or in the full mix?

#deathmetal #mastering #metalmastering #mixingmastering #audioengineering

Your black metal mix is too narrow.

Only the sides, for 22 seconds. That's everything that differs between left and right, and next to the middle the master has 2.8 dB more of it, so the guitars stop sitting on top of the vocals and wrap around them.

Then the full stereo master at -12.5 LUFS.

It's Frostbound Sepulchre by Vesper Mortis.

Did the sides jump out more on headphones or speakers?
